questions.question:
‘A @ B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’

‘A & B’ means ‘A is the father of B’

‘A # B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’

Which of the following options means 'P is the mother of L'?
questions.solution:
Family Chart:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2a776c0a19b6706031165c847bcb98978a1e150482bd1260c12a74559ea55407.png] 

Decoding the Symbols:

 
 

 Symbol
 @
 &
 #
 
 

 Meaning
 Wife
 Father
 Sister
 
 

 

Option 1: S @ L & R # P

It means: S is the Wife of L, L is the Father of R, R is the Sister of P.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/04ec44f910db055c07e8dcee950c4d4d3e86bcb6bbca4c2e030fddd93141c36f.png] 

Here, P is the Child of L.

**Option 2: P @ R & S # L**

It means: P is the Wife of R, R is the Father of S, S is the Sister of L.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0b2f2830d28bc186973c3284b4b1cfec37053db24c2273f54171f337444c4e24.png] 

**Here, P is the Mother of L.**

Option 3: P @ L & S # R 

It means: P is the Wife of L, L is the Father of S, S is the Sister of R.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f795ef36fbaacb1b30941feebd4b22f553e221731cd5155cc09fc955663e333.png] 

Here, P is the wife of L.

Option 4: S @ P # R & L 

It means: S is the Wife of P, P is the Sister of R, R is the Father of L.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7f849c2f01918870310f3e0a1d8f267c9962c582bbdb43b749060f81b9a82c58.png] 

Since, P is the Husband of S, so P is a male therefore, P can't be the sister of R.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.)

Arc : Circle : : Cockpit : ?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: **The second word is the larger construct or whole which contains the first word.**

Here,

Arc : Circle → An **arc** is part of a **circle**.

Similarly,

Cockpit : Airplane → A **cockpit** is part of an **airplane**.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Airplane"**.

questions.question: In a certain code language, ‘PROVED’ is written as ‘65’and ‘REMOVER’ is written as ‘81’.How will ‘DEVOUR’ be written in that language?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c6e81f3ed21fddc72dd7e74439132a9341e1cd67dad9da66ee032ef789862eab.png] 

The logic followed here is:

Logic: Sum of the place value of all the letters except O.

'PROVED’ is written as ‘65'

⇒ 16 + 18 + 22 + 5 + 4 = 65.

'REMOVER’ is written as ‘81'

⇒ 18 + 5 + 13 + 22 + 5 + 18 = 81.

Similarly, for '**DEVOUR**'

⇒ 4 + 5 + 22 + 21 + 18 = 70.

So, 'DEVOUR' will be written as '70'.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

questions.question:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered 1, 2 and 3. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

1. All cottons are silks.

2. All silks are wools.

3. All wools are jutes.

Conclusions:

1. Some jutes are silks.

2. Some wools are cottons.

3. Some jutes are cottons.
questions.solution:
Given Statements:

1. All cottons are silks.

2. All silks are wools.

3. All wools are jutes.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0081d7883aa874bee933623e46710cf9f3b5710ff89b40b4016ef171497ba3e4.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some jutes are silks - True (Because, All silks are wools and All wools are jutes, so Some jutes are silks will be definitely true).

II. Some wools are cottons - True (Because, All cottons are silks and All silks are wools, so Some wools are cottons will be definitely true).

III. Some jutes are cottons - True (Because, All silks are wools, All wools are jutes and All wools are jutes, so Some jutes are cottons will be definitely true).

So, All conclusions 1, 2 and 3 follow.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number.

2 : 1 : : 54 : 3 : : 16 : ?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: (2nd number)³ **× 2 = 1st number.**

Now,

For, 2 : 1

⇒ (1)³ × 2

⇒ 1 × 2 = 2.

For, 54 : 3

⇒ (3)3 × 2

⇒ 27 × 2 = 54.

Similarly, for **16 : ?**

**⇒ (2)3 × 2**

**⇒ 8 × 2 = 16.**

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must NOT be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word)

Engineer : build : : Physician : ______
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: **The second word is a common action or task performed by the first word.**

Here,

Engineer : Build → An **engineer **typically **builds **or designs things.

Similarly,

Physician : Cure → A **physician **typically **cures **or treats patients.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Cure"**.
